plain: To mix things up or confuse them so they cannot be told apart.

webster.text: To mingle and blend different things, so that their forms or natures cannot be distinguished; to mix in a mass or crowd, so that individuals cannot be distinguished.

more.text: To abash; to throw the mind into disorder; to cast down; to make ashamed.

example.quote: Men, upon too many occasions, do not give their own understandings fair play; but, yielding to some untoward bias, they entangle themselves in words and confound themselves in subtleties.
